page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-1xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server configured on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 20 physical cores and 20 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, utilizing a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.8 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is delivered by a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, which includes 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is consistently strong across both small and large block read/write operations, though the PassMark memory score falls in the average tier. The instance demonstrates exceptional capabilities in text and image processing, as well as single-threaded compression and decompression, all scoring in the top 10%.

The integrated NVIDIA L40S GPU with 48 GB VRAM provides substantial acceleration for machine learning workloads. LLM inference benchmarks show top-tier performance for small 135M models, achieving over 4400 tokens per second for prompt processing and 386 tokens per second for text generation. For medium 7B models, text generation remains strong, while prompt processing and larger 70B model inference operate at average performance tiers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a high density of system memory and GPU VRAM relative to its 20 vCPU allocation, making it a viable option for resource-intensive workloads without requiring a higher vCPU tier. Due to the lack of local storage, external storage solutions must be utilized. This configuration is highly suitable for medium-scale LLM inference, data science pipelines, image processing, and parallelized compute workloads that leverage GPU acceleration.
